answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make every identity stake a scarce resource before it trades, like a cedar that only grows after years of slow investment. A newcomer posts a deposit that is slashed for misbehavior, so launching a tide of fake identities costs real money instead of nothing. Random peer audits then verify each agent actually does work, the way a walnut proves a tree is real: a fake identity has nothing to crack open. Attackers pay per identity; honest agents pay once and keep trading.
